extraction_note: FTAI's 10-K describes a commercial aerospace aftermarket business focused on CFM56-5B / CFM56-7B / V2500 engines powering 737NG and A320ceo aircraft. Despite the cohort metadata flagging 'some military adjacency via leasing structures' and 'LM2500 marine', the FY2025 10-K contains NO specific Pentagon Program Element references, NO named DoD programs of record, NO PE-number citations, and NO DoD-customer revenue concentration disclosures. Customer concentration (13%, 10%, 23% AR) is disclosed only at the Aerospace Products segment level without naming customers. The two prior LM2500-marine and offshore-energy lines are referenced only as legacy/wind-down items in commitments/contingencies. As a result, J-Book-grounded claims are absent and the J-Book divergence pattern is structurally inapplicable to this filing. Claims below capture the narrative drivers actually present (commercial engine MRE, Strategic Capital Initiative, leasing utilization) plus the residual offshore-energy contingency for completeness.
